title: Auto-Pigeon incident envelope 1.0
description: The one shape every Auto-Pigeon component reports a user-impacting incident in. Deliberately CLOSED: additionalProperties is false at every level and `evidence` is a fixed set of typed counters, so no request body, no map document, no annotation text and no prefab content can travel inside an incident even by accident. Anything a component wants to report that this schema cannot express is a schema change, reviewed here, rather than a free-form field.

schema_version.description: The version of THIS envelope contract, not of any component. Present in every event so a receiver reading a mixed backlog knows which rules the record was written under.

incident_id.description: Identifies one incident. Stable across escalations: the 3s, 10s and 30s notifications about one stall are one incident_id, so a receiver groups rather than counts four outages.

occurred_at.description: When the incident STARTED, in UTC, RFC 3339 with milliseconds. Not when it was reported and not when it was received — an escalation reports the same start.

severity.description: warning: the product still works and the user is being told something is slow or degraded. error: this operation failed but the session is usable. fatal: this session may no longer be reliable — the only severity that earns the fatal modal.

component.description: Which repository's code raised it. The acronyms are the workspace's own and are the same strings the version manifest and the health dashboard use.

subsystem.description: The part of that component, in its own vocabulary: `render.3d`, `scheduler`, `room`, `wad`, `journal`. Free text on purpose — a closed list here would need editing for every new subsystem — but it is an identifier, never a sentence, and it is length-bounded so it cannot become a dumping ground.

code.description: A canonical incident code from incident-codes.json. Extending the taxonomy means adding to that file, which is what makes 'which errors exist' answerable without reading six repositories.

operation.description: The user-recognisable operation in flight — `Paste`, `Bend`, `extract.textures`, `session.join`. This is what makes a message truthful about what the user was doing; it is not a stack frame and not a URL.

message.description: One sentence a user could be shown. Redaction runs over it (see redaction-rules.json), but redaction is the safety net — the writer's duty is not to put an address, an email or a path in here in the first place.

duration_ms.description: How long the operation had been running when the incident was raised. Doctrine pillar 2: a duration is evidence and a message without one is an opinion.

correlation_id.description: The cross-stack correlation id (see correlation.mjs). One user action carries one value through AUP -> AUB -> AUE/AUC, so four components' incidents about one failure can be read as one story.

release.description: The reporting component's own `1.<commit-count>` release, exactly as PREPROD-05 derives it. `unknown` is a permitted, meaningful value: an uninjected build says so rather than inventing a placeholder version that gets believed.

environment.description: Which deployment this came from. Sent as GlitchTip's `environment` so a development stack's noise never has to be read alongside production's.

recoverable.description: Whether the session can carry on. false is what escalates a report to the fatal modal, so it is a deliberate claim by the writer rather than a consequence of severity.

user_action.description: What the reader can actually do — `Reload the page`, `Wait or reload`, `Sign in again`. Omitted when there is honestly nothing to suggest; an invented suggestion is worse than none.

evidence.description: The typed, bounded facts an incident may carry. Every member is a NUMBER or a short controlled string, and additionalProperties is false — which is the whole point. A map document, a request body, a WAD, an annotation or a prefab cannot be expressed here, so no code path can smuggle one in and no reviewer has to check that it did not.

brush_count.description: Brushes affected by the operation that failed or stalled.

face_count.description: Faces affected. `31,040 faces are affected` is the difference between a truthful warning and a spinner.

triangle_count.description: Triangles the renderer was asked to draw.

selection_count.description: Objects in the selection the operation ran over.

http_status.description: The HTTP status a refusing service answered with.

http_reason.description: The service's own short reason CODE — `map_not_found`, `session_full` — never a response body and never a message built from one.

queue_depth.description: Items waiting when the incident was raised: AUB's job queue, AUC's outbound buffer.

worker_attempt.description: Which attempt this was, 1-based. Distinguishes `failed once and retried` from `failed four times`.

client_count.description: Clients in the room, for AUC capacity and backpressure incidents.

retry_after_ms.description: How long the client was told to wait before retrying.

event_loop_lag_ms.description: Measured event-loop lag on a Node service, or main-thread stall as measured by the worker heartbeat in a browser.

memory_mb.description: Resident memory at the moment of the incident, in MiB.
